name: Manufacturing

bnote.101002: HMA Agro is India's largest listed buffalo-meat exporter. The others are the world's largest listed beef processors.
bnote.104003: India's two largest listed edible-oil companies, then global oilseed processors.
bnote.106101: Listed Indian basmati and rice millers.
bnote.107201: Five listed Indian cane-sugar makers. Most also make ethanol and power.
bnote.107302: No chocolate maker is listed in India; Cadbury India is a subsidiary of Mondelez.
bnote.107901: No listed Indian infant-formula pure-play; Nestlé is the global leader.
bnote.110101: Indian whisky leaders first, then global spirits majors.
bnote.110106: Indian distillers whose volume is largely country liquor and extra-neutral alcohol.
bnote.120099: Altria sells oral nicotine pouches and smokeless tobacco. Japan Tobacco is mainly cigarettes and is placed here because the cigarette slot is full.
bnote.131104: Listed Indian jute mills. Ludlow Jute could not be read from the data source.
bnote.141001: Vedant Fashions (Manyavar) designs and sells ethnic wear; most making is outsourced. Closest listed match.
bnote.141099: Global apparel brand owners. Most outsource manufacturing.
bnote.151201: Indian luggage leaders first, then global luggage and handbag makers.
bnote.152002: Indian non-leather footwear leaders, then global sportswear brands.
bnote.170101: Five listed Indian writing and printing paper makers.
bnote.170102: No listed newsprint pure-play in India; Norske Skog is one of the last large listed newsprint makers.
bnote.201106: Five listed Indian specialty and fluorine chemical makers.
bnote.210002: India's five largest listed formulation makers by revenue.
bnote.210099: More large Indian formulation makers, placed here because the formulations slot is full.
bnote.210003: No sizeable listed Ayush pure-play found; the big Ayurveda brands sit inside Dabur, Emami and Patanjali.
bnote.222004: Five listed Indian PVC pipe makers.
bnote.239401: India's five largest listed cement makers.
bnote.239499: More Indian cement makers, placed here because the main cement slot is full.
bnote.239501: Global building-materials majors with large ready-mix and precast concrete businesses.
bnote.241003: India's four largest listed steelmakers, then ArcelorMittal.
bnote.251301: BHEL and Thermax build boilers and steam generators in India.
bnote.252000: Bharat Dynamics makes missiles and munitions; Rheinmetall is Europe's largest listed ammunition maker.
bnote.261101: India's listed solar cell and module makers, then First Solar, the largest US maker.
bnote.261102: Saatvik assembles modules in India. JinkoSolar and Canadian Solar are among the largest module makers globally.
bnote.261103: No listed Indian inverter maker found. Sungrow, Enphase, SolarEdge and SMA are the main listed players abroad.
bnote.261901: Murata and TDK are the world's largest passive-component makers. Vishay makes resistors, capacitors and discrete devices.
bnote.261902: SPEL is India's only listed semiconductor assembly and test unit, and it is tiny. onsemi and Diodes are discrete and power-chip makers.
bnote.261903: No listed Indian chip maker. These five are the largest analog and microcontroller makers.
bnote.261904: India's listed electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and PCB-assembly companies.
bnote.261905: No listed Indian display maker. BOE and Sharp make display panels; Universal Display licenses OLED materials.
bnote.261906: No listed Indian chip fab. TSMC, Intel and Micron run fabs; NVIDIA and AMD design processors and outsource manufacturing.
bnote.261907: Indian defence and space electronics makers.
bnote.261908: No Indian pure-play. Amphenol and TE Connectivity are the largest connector and cable-assembly makers.
bnote.262001: No listed Indian PC maker. Lenovo, Dell and HP are the three largest PC makers.
bnote.262099: Netweb builds servers and supercomputers in India. Super Micro and HPE are large server makers.
bnote.263001: Dixon assembles phones for brands in India. Apple and Xiaomi are the main listed phone makers.
bnote.263003: No listed Indian router or switch maker. Cisco, Arista and Fortinet lead networking and firewalls.
bnote.263007: HFCL and Tejas make optical and transmission equipment in India.
bnote.263008: No listed Indian RAN maker. Ericsson and Nokia are the two main 4G/5G network vendors outside China.
bnote.265103: Genus and HPL make electricity meters in India, including smart meters.
bnote.265105: Bharat Electronics makes radars and defence electronics. Garmin and Trimble lead satellite navigation.
bnote.265106: No listed Indian lab-instrument maker. These are the four largest abroad.
bnote.265107: Honeywell Automation India is the main listed Indian process-control company.
bnote.265201: No listed Indian watchmaker with clean data (Titan's watches are inside a jewellery business, listed under jewellery).
bnote.271002: Listed Indian transformer and grid-equipment makers.
bnote.271003: CG Power and ABB India make motors in India. WEG and Nidec are large motor makers abroad.
bnote.271004: No listed Indian electrolyser maker. These are listed electrolyser makers in Europe and the US; all are loss-making.
bnote.272002: India's lead-acid and lithium battery makers, then CATL, the world's largest EV battery maker.
bnote.273201: India's five largest listed wire and cable makers.
bnote.275003: India's listed air-conditioner and cooler makers, plus Daikin.
bnote.281105: Suzlon and Inox Wind make wind turbines in India. Vestas and Nordex are the largest listed makers in Europe.
bnote.281302: Listed Indian pump makers, plus Xylem.
bnote.281401: India's listed bearing makers. Their foreign parents are left out to avoid counting a company twice.
bnote.282101: Mahindra & Mahindra is India's largest tractor maker (it also makes cars). Deere and CNH are the largest abroad.
bnote.282999: No listed Indian semiconductor-equipment maker. These five supply most of the world's chip-making machines.
bnote.291001: India's three largest listed car makers, then Toyota and Tesla.
bnote.291003: Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors (commercial vehicles) lead Indian trucks. Volvo, Daimler Truck and PACCAR lead abroad.
bnote.301102: India's listed defence shipyards, plus Huntington Ingalls, the largest US naval shipbuilder.
bnote.302003: India's listed wagon and coach makers, plus Greenbrier from the US.
bnote.303001: HAL is India's only listed aircraft maker.
bnote.303006: Azad and Unimech make precision aerospace parts in India. Safran, GE Aerospace and Rolls-Royce lead jet engines.
bnote.321101: India's largest listed jewellery makers and retailers.
bnote.329001: India's listed pen and stationery makers, plus BIC.
bnote.331500: No listed Indian MRO pure-play. AAR and ST Engineering run large aircraft and ship repair businesses.

flags.itc: Diversified: cigarettes, FMCG, paper and agri. Cigarettes earn most of the profit.
flags.eidparry: Consolidated figures include Coromandel International (fertilisers), which dominates revenue.
flags.tcpl: Diversified: tea, coffee, salt, foods and Starbucks India.
flags.nestle: Diversified global food group. Figures in Swiss francs.
flags.hma: Net profit is above EBITDA, so it includes non-operating income.
flags.tilaknagar: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.som: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.prataap: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.freshpet: Net profit includes a tax benefit.
flags.mkc: Net profit includes a one-off gain.
flags.repro: Net profit includes a large one-off gain.
flags.kitex: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.raymondlsl: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.ip: Loss reflects restructuring and mill-closure charges.
flags.tapestry: ROE is inflated by buybacks that shrank equity.
flags.jeld: Heavy losses; equity is nearly wiped out.
flags.norske: Net profit despite negative EBITDA comes from one-off gains.
flags.ivl: Thai polyester and PET giant; loss-making in the trailing year.
flags.reliance: Diversified: refining and petrochemicals, retail and Jio telecom. Figures are for the whole group.
flags.grasim: Consolidated figures include UltraTech Cement and Aditya Birla Capital.
flags.kiri: Net profit includes a very large one-off gain, so the profit margin and P/E are not operating.
flags.hul: Net profit includes a one-off gain, so the profit margin is not operating.
flags.jswdulux: Net profit includes a one-off gain; renamed after JSW bought Akzo Nobel India.
flags.tatachem: Loss reflects impairments in overseas soda ash.
flags.dcmshriram: Diversified: chlor-alkali, sugar, fertiliser and others.
flags.premier: Net profit is above EBITDA, so it includes other income.
flags.moderna: Revenue has collapsed after the pandemic; deep losses.
flags.esteelauder: Near-zero TTM profit makes the P/E meaningless.
flags.lindeindia: Very high P/E for a gases company; check the source page.
flags.hindalco: Consolidated figures include Novelis (US/Europe aluminium rolling).
flags.tatasteel: Consolidated figures include Tata Steel Europe.
flags.birlanu: Renamed from HIL; loss-making in the trailing year.
flags.ramcoind: Net profit includes its share of Ramco Cements' profit.
flags.maithan: Net profit is above EBITDA because of large treasury income.
flags.mukand: Net profit includes a large one-off gain.
flags.bdl: Net profit is above EBITDA because of large interest income on cash.
flags.aiaeng: Net profit roughly equals EBITDA because of large treasury income.
flags.centuryalu: Net profit includes a one-off gain.
flags.holcim: Profit reflects the 2025 spin-off of its North American business (Amrize).
flags.tmpv: FY26 net profit includes a large one-time gain from the Tata Motors demerger, so net margin and P/E are not operating results.
flags.wdc: Net profit includes a large gain from the Sandisk separation, so net margin is not an operating figure.
flags.spel: Very small company with almost no revenue.
flags.sony: Net income in the source is negative because of one-off items; EBITDA is positive.
flags.tejasnet: Tejas had a sharp fall in orders and is loss-making in the latest twelve months.
flags.swatch: Profit fell almost to zero, so the P/E is not meaningful.
flags.hni: HNI completed a large acquisition (Steelcase), so its latest profit is depressed.
flags.ideaforge: Profit is close to zero, so the P/E is not meaningful.
flags.centum: ROCE and ROE in the source do not match its net loss; treat them with care.
flags.ba: Boeing's EBITDA is negative, and its equity is negative, so ROE is not shown.

notes: All divisions 10 to 33 are mapped. Where India has no listed company in a niche, listed companies abroad are used.
